content.text: The excerpt reviews liver and pancreatic diseases. It discusses acute yellow atrophy, its causes, pregnancy association, pathology, jaundice, neurological symptoms, hemorrhage, diagnosis, and largely unsuccessful treatment; phosphorus poisoning closely resembles it. It then covers liver cancer, amyloid and fatty degeneration, biliary catarrh, gallstones, hepatic colic, duct obstruction, portal thrombosis and pylephlebitis, echinococcal and liver-fluke infections, and their diagnosis and historical treatments. Gallstones arise through bile stasis, mucus, altered chemistry, and dietary or constitutional factors, producing severe colic and sometimes jaundice. Pancreatic sections describe anatomy, digestive function, pancreatitis, chronic inflammation, cancer, malabsorption, steatorrhea, emaciation, pain, jaundice, and palliative or enzyme-replacement treatment. Sandra went to the garden.
